Netanyahu calls Trump 'by far, the greatest friend Israel has ever had'
item.description:
Netanyahu calls Trump 'by far, the greatest friend Israel has ever had'

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called US President Donald Trump “by far, the greatest friend Israel has ever had”, in footage he shared a day after Trump endorsed him ahead of Israel’s upcoming elections.

On Sunday, Trump praised Netanyahu as a “great warrior prime minister” and a partner for peace, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February.

The conflict, now in its seventh month, has disrupted global energy markets and caused widespread damage across the Middle East, including to critical infrastructure and regional economies.

item.title: Egyptian construction firms surveyed sites in Gaza for 'Green Rafah' project, sources say
item.description:
Egyptian construction firms surveyed sites in Gaza for 'Green Rafah' project, sources say

Egyptian construction firms surveyed sites in the ruins of the southern Gaza Strip for a housing project dubbed "Green Rafah", Egyptian sources have told Middle East Eye.

A senior military source based in Egypt's North Sinai province told MEE that Egyptian engineers surveyed several areas in eastern Rafah under the supervision of the Israeli army and air force, who accompanied them throughout the process until they left the besieged Palestinian enclave.

Rafah was once home to roughly 250,000 Palestinians and known for its bustling local markets, refugee camps, and surrounding green spaces.

But since Israel launched its genocidal war on the enclave, Israeli forces have demolished at least 80 percent of the buildings in the governorate, with nearly all of its former residents now rendered homeless.

Speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak to the media, the source said that "the proposed neighbourhood would initially house around 20,000 Palestinians and be supervised by a multinational force expected to be deployed in several parts of the Gaza Strip under the Sharm el-Sheikh peace agreement.

Read more: Egyptian construction firms surveyed sites in Gaza for 'Green Rafah' project, sources say

item.title: Trump says Nato 'weren't there to help' during war on Iran
item.description:
Trump says Nato 'weren't there to help' during war on Iran

US President Donald Trump has slammed Nato allies, saying they "weren't there to help" Washington during its war on Iran. 

"We stand with Europe despite its flaws, its weaknesses…But if they don't soon find their way, and they have to find their way, we will have no choice but to leave," he said at a campaign rally.

"We spend hundreds of billions of dollars a year on Nato protecting them, but when we said, 'Would you like to help?' 'No, thank you.' 'Oh, no thank you?' What does that mean, 'No, thank you'?"

Trump added that the US spent "so much money on Nato", adding that they "weren't there to help" and that its something Washington "can never really forget".

item.title: How to Sell a Genocide: The Media’s Complicity in the Destruction of Gaza
item.description: The dispute over whether Israel’s assault on Gaza amounts to genocide has largely been settled. Amnesty International, a UN commission of inquiry and the International Association of Genocide Scholars have all reached that conclusion, as have many leading scholars of genocide. The question that remains is how the greatest political crime of our time was allowed to happen. Adam H. Johnson’s How to Sell a Genocide goes a long way to explaining it. Published by Pluto Press with a foreword by the Palestinian American human rights lawyer Noura Erakat, the book covers the crucial period from October 2023 to October 2024, when Western audiences were primed for genocide. Johnson shows that the mainstream American media did much of the priming. […]

item.title: Israel violating US-mediated framework agreement, Lebanese president says
item.description: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said Monday that Israel has failed to comply with a US-mediated framework agreement signed in June and continues daily violations in southern Lebanon, reaffirming his country’s commitment to a diplomatic solution, Anadolu reports. Aoun made the remarks during a meeting with Arab League Secretary-General Nabil Fahmy at the presidential palace in Baabda, east of Beirut, according to a statement from the Lebanese presidency. “The Israelis have not adhered to the framework agreement, and the south continues to face daily violations,” Aoun said. He stressed that continued Israeli violations would not achieve their objectives but would instead strengthen the Lebanese people’s determination to defend their land and rights. item.title: Iran says 20 to 30 aircraft destroyed during war with US, Israel
item.description: Between 20 and 30 aircraft were destroyed during Iran’s war with the US and Israel, the head of the country’s state-owned flag carrier said Monday, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. Taher Abdolhai, CEO of Iran Air, also known as HOMA, said at a news conference that Iran needs approximately 1,000 passenger aircraft but currently has only around 300. Of those, between 130 and 140 aircraft were operational before the war, with 20 to 30 destroyed during the conflict, he said. Abdolhai also said between 70 and 80 aircraft were targeted during the war. He claimed Israeli attacks had caused particularly severe damage to Iran Air aircraft, saying some planes belonging to other operators were struck by single missiles, […]

item.title: UK threatens sanctions against firms linked to Israel’s illegal settlements in West Bank
item.description: British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on Monday warned companies and individuals against bidding for construction projects linked to illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, citing potential sanctions, Anadolu reports. “We urge businesses and individuals not to proceed with bids for E1 construction tenders,” Miliband said in a statement. He warned that participation in the project could carry legal and reputational consequences, including the risk of involvement in serious breaches of international law. “I want to be very clear with those considering engaging in the tendering process: we have created new powers allowing us to sanction individuals and companies involved in the construction of illegal settlements such as E1,” Miliband said.
